content.title: Flash flood: turn around route
content.summary: Floodwater blocks the road you expected to use. Practice choosing a route without crossing water or a barricade.
content.objective: Practice turning around at floodwater and using official information to choose a safer route.

sources.label: National Weather Service — During a Flood
National Weather Service — Before a Flood
National Weather Service — Flood Warning vs. Watch
National Weather Service — Turn Around Don't Drown

avoided_floodwater.text: You kept the vehicle and everyone in it out of floodwater.

followed_road_closure.text: You treated the barricade as a closed route and stayed away from it.

recognized_official_source.text: You used official alerts and road closures to guide the next move.

needs_route_review.text: Identify another route that avoids low crossings and flood-prone roads.

nodes.title: Water covers the road
nodes.body: You are stopped before a low crossing. Water is moving across the road, and you cannot see the pavement underneath.

choices.label: Turn around without entering the water
choices.consequence: You stay on dry pavement and put distance between the vehicle and the crossing.
choices.feedback: The National Weather Service says never to drive or walk into floodwater. Water can hide a washed-out road and other hazards.

choices.label: Wait to see whether another vehicle makes it through
choices.consequence: The water keeps moving, and another driver's attempt cannot show what is safe for you.
choices.feedback: You cannot judge the water's depth or the road beneath it by watching another vehicle. The National Weather Service says water may be deeper than it appears.

choices.label: Ease forward to test how deep the water is
choices.consequence: The water's depth and the condition of the road are still hidden.
choices.feedback: The National Weather Service says it is never safe to drive into floodwater. Turn around before the vehicle enters it.

nodes.scene: 6:15 PM · Heavy rain on the drive home

nodes.title: Choose another route
nodes.body: From a dry, higher parking area, you need another way around. A map still shows the usual road, but an official flash flood warning is active.

choices.label: Check official alerts and road-closure information
choices.consequence: The official update shows a marked detour away from the low crossing.
choices.feedback: Flood conditions can change quickly. The National Weather Service recommends staying informed through radio, television, and official alerts, and obeying evacuation orders.

choices.label: Take the familiar shortcut through another low spot
choices.consequence: That route also leads toward low ground where water can collect.
choices.feedback: A familiar road can still flood. The National Weather Service recommends knowing where water collects and how to reach higher ground.

choices.label: Follow an unverified post that says a shortcut is open
choices.consequence: The post does not show when the route was checked or whether conditions changed.
choices.feedback: Use current official alerts and closures for a fast-changing flood rather than relying on an unverified route report.

nodes.title: A road-closed barricade ahead
nodes.body: The next intersection has a road-closed barricade. The marked detour is longer, and the road beyond the barrier looks dry from where you are stopped. A dry parking area on higher ground is a short distance back.

choices.label: Stay behind the barricade and take the marked detour
choices.consequence: You remain on the open route and continue away from the closed road.
choices.feedback: The National Weather Service says not to drive around a flood barricade. The road beyond it may have collapsed under the water.

choices.label: Go back to the dry, higher parking area and wait for an official update
choices.consequence: You move away from the closed road and check whether the route changes.
choices.feedback: Moving to a dry, higher place keeps you away from floodwater while you monitor official information. The National Weather Service says to stay informed during a flood.

choices.label: Go around the barricade because the pavement looks dry
choices.consequence: The barrier still marks the road as closed, including hazards you cannot see from here.
choices.feedback: Do not drive around a barricade. Floodwater, a washed-out road, or another hazard may be beyond your view.

outcomes.title: You practiced the turn-around decision
outcomes.body: You walked through the same pattern at three decision points: stay out of floodwater, use current official information, and treat barricades as closed routes.
